title: Restriction normalization of a binary comparison composite
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_Y^e$ be categories [def-nagata-category], for $Y=X,S,T$ and $e=r,s$. Products of functors below mean functional composition; all associators are inserted. For $k=a:S\to X$, $b:T\to S$, and $ab:T\to X$ give functors $L_k^e:\mathcal C_{\operatorname{target}(k)}^e\to\mathcal C_{\operatorname{source}(k)}^e$ and $E_k^e$ in the opposite direction, and natural isomorphisms $\rho_k^e:L_k^eE_k^e\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Give coherent identifications $L_{ab}^e\cong L_b^eL_a^e$ and natural isomorphisms $\gamma_{a,b}^e:E_a^eE_b^e\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{ab}^e$ satisfying, under those identifications,
$$\rho_{ab}^e\circ L_{ab}^e(\gamma_{a,b}^e)=\rho_b^e\circ L_b^e(\rho_a^e E_b^e).\tag{G}$$
Give functors $F_Y:\mathcal C_Y^r\to\mathcal C_Y^s$ and natural isomorphisms $q_k:L_k^sF_{\operatorname{target}(k)}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\operatorname{source}(k)}L_k^r$ with
$$q_{ab}=(q_bL_a^r)\circ L_b^s(q_a).$$
Give natural isomorphisms $h_a:F_XE_a^r\xrightarrow{\sim}E_a^sF_S$ and $h_b:F_SE_b^r\xrightarrow{\sim}E_b^sF_T$ satisfying, for $k=a,b$,
$$\rho_k^sF_{\operatorname{source}(k)}\circ L_k^s(h_k)=F_{\operatorname{source}(k)}(\rho_k^r)\circ(q_kE_k^r).\tag{N}$$
Set $H=(E_a^sh_b)\circ(h_aE_b^r)$ and $\eta^e=\rho_b^e\circ L_b^e(\rho_a^eE_b^e)$. Then the following equality of natural transformations holds:
$$\eta^sF_T\circ L_b^sL_a^s(H)=F_T(\eta^r)\circ(q_bL_a^rE_a^rE_b^r)\circ L_b^s(q_aE_a^rE_b^r).\tag{B}$$
Furthermore the natural isomorphism
$$\widetilde h_{ab}=\gamma_{a,b}^sF_T\circ H\circ F_X((\gamma_{a,b}^r)^{-1}):F_XE_{ab}^r\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{ab}^sF_T$$
is normalized, that is,
$$\rho_{ab}^sF_T\circ L_{ab}^s(\widetilde h_{ab})=F_T(\rho_{ab}^r)\circ(q_{ab}E_{ab}^r).$$
No faithfulness, adjunction, or geometry is assumed.

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition: restriction calculation (G), (N), (B), isolated from returned parent steps 1 and 3; agent-extracted formal calculation, not a separate Stacks theorem

proof.text:
Work componentwise at an arbitrary $M\in\mathcal C_T^r$, with the coherent restriction identifications in the statement understood. Put $P=E_b^rM$, $u=(h_b)_M:F_SP\to E_b^sF_TM$, and $v=(\rho_a^r)_P:L_a^rE_a^rP\to P$. Composition below is right to left. Let $A_M$ be the component of the left side of (B). Expanding $H$ and $\eta^s$, functoriality gives
$$A_M=(\rho_b^s)_{F_TM}\circ L_b^s\bigl((\rho_a^s)_{E_b^sF_TM}\circ L_a^sE_a^s(u)\circ L_a^s((h_a)_P)\bigr).$$
Apply the exchange identity of [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] with inner transformation $h_b:F_SE_b^r\Rightarrow E_b^sF_T$ and outer transformation $\rho_a^s:L_a^sE_a^s\Rightarrow1$. At $M$ it reads
$$(\rho_a^s)_{E_b^sF_TM}\circ L_a^sE_a^s(u)=u\circ(\rho_a^s)_{F_SP}.$$
Consequently
$$A_M=(\rho_b^s)_{F_TM}\circ L_b^s(u)\circ L_b^s\bigl((\rho_a^s)_{F_SP}\circ L_a^s((h_a)_P)\bigr).$$

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition; explicit agent calculation, step 1

proof.text:
Use (N) for $a$ at $P$, then (N) for $b$ at $M$. These are respectively
$$(\rho_a^s)_{F_SP}\circ L_a^s((h_a)_P)=F_S(v)\circ(q_a)_{E_a^rP},$$
$$(\rho_b^s)_{F_TM}\circ L_b^s(u)=F_T((\rho_b^r)_M)\circ(q_b)_P.$$
Substitution in the expression from step 1, distributing $L_b^s$ over the composite, gives
$$A_M=F_T((\rho_b^r)_M)\circ(q_b)_P\circ L_b^sF_S(v)\circ L_b^s((q_a)_{E_a^rP}).$$
Only the two assumed normalizations, functoriality and associativity [def-nagata-category] were used.

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition; explicit agent calculation, step 2

proof.text:
The exchange identity [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange], with inner transformation $\rho_a^r E_b^r:L_a^rE_a^rE_b^r\Rightarrow E_b^r$ and outer transformation $q_b:L_b^sF_S\Rightarrow F_TL_b^r$, gives at $M$
$$(q_b)_P\circ L_b^sF_S(v)=F_TL_b^r(v)\circ(q_b)_{L_a^rE_a^rP}.$$
Both arguments of $q_b$ lie in $\mathcal C_S^r$, the category in which $v$ is a morphism; this is its ordinary naturality square.

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition; explicit agent calculation, step 3

proof.text:
Insert step 3 into step 2 and combine the two adjacent images under $F_T$. By the definition of $\eta^r$,
$$A_M=F_T\bigl((\rho_b^r)_M\circ L_b^r(v)\bigr)\circ(q_b)_{L_a^rE_a^rP}\circ L_b^s((q_a)_{E_a^rP})
=F_T((\eta^r)_M)\circ(q_b)_{L_a^rE_a^rE_b^rM}\circ L_b^s((q_a)_{E_a^rE_b^rM}).$$
This is exactly the component of the right side of (B). Equality of components is equality of natural transformations (a natural transformation is precisely its family of components). This proves (B), using functoriality and the category laws [def-nagata-category].

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition; explicit agent calculation, step 4

proof.text:
Put $D^e=L_b^eL_a^e$ and $Q=q_{ab}$, using the supplied coherent identification $L_{ab}^e\cong D^e$. For $M\in\mathcal C_T^r$ write $w_M=((\gamma_{a,b}^r)^{-1})_M:E_{ab}^rM\to E_a^rE_b^rM$, and let $C_M$ denote the component of $\rho_{ab}^sF_T\circ L_{ab}^s(\widetilde h_{ab})$. Expanding $\widetilde h_{ab}$ and using (G) for $s$ at $F_TM$ yields
$$C_M=(\eta^s)_{F_TM}\circ D^s(H_M)\circ D^sF_X(w_M).$$
Apply (B), already proved in steps 1--4, and the assumed formula $Q=(q_bL_a^r)\circ L_b^s(q_a)$, to obtain
$$C_M=F_T((\eta^r)_M)\circ Q_{E_a^rE_b^rM}\circ D^sF_X(w_M).$$
These are substitutions of the hypotheses and of the earlier equality, with reassociation [def-nagata-category].

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition; explicit agent calculation, step 5

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] to the inner transformation $(\gamma_{a,b}^r)^{-1}:E_{ab}^r\Rightarrow E_a^rE_b^r$ and outer transformation $Q:D^sF_X\Rightarrow F_TD^r$. Its component at $M$ states
$$Q_{E_a^rE_b^rM}\circ D^sF_X(w_M)=F_TD^r(w_M)\circ Q_{E_{ab}^rM}.$$
Thus step 5 becomes
$$C_M=F_T\bigl((\eta^r)_M\circ D^r(w_M)\bigr)\circ Q_{E_{ab}^rM}.$$
Here $w_M$ is a morphism of $\mathcal C_X^r$, exactly the domain of $Q$; no interchange of unrelated component categories is made.

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition; explicit agent calculation, step 6

proof.text:
By (G) for $r$, $(\eta^r)_M=(\rho_{ab}^r)_M\circ D^r((\gamma_{a,b}^r)_M)$. Since $w_M$ is its specified inverse compositor, functoriality and the inverse identities give
$$(\eta^r)_M\circ D^r(w_M)=(\rho_{ab}^r)_M\circ D^r((\gamma_{a,b}^r)_M\circ w_M)=(\rho_{ab}^r)_M.$$
Step 6 therefore reads
$$C_M=F_T((\rho_{ab}^r)_M)\circ(q_{ab})_{E_{ab}^rM},$$
which is the asserted normalization component, for arbitrary $M$. The displayed $\widetilde h_{ab}$ is a natural isomorphism: whiskering an isomorphism has as inverse the whiskered inverse (a functor preserves the two inverse equations), and the inverse of a composite is the reversed composite of inverses. This also verifies the isomorphism assertion. Everything in this step is functoriality, the inverse equations and the category laws [def-nagata-category].
